sourceFile: "Weekly Cycle of Prayer 2026.pdf", provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 1DTuMBQq3vNVw2AXOVSnlBXROs3L8apiF, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer"). A companion daily-cadence file for the same diocese also exists in the same folder (file id 1ALpNslzzYggcEUQWZJRwYGKQ5cINKfGq, "Daily Cycle of Prayer 2026.pdf") -- the roster spreadsheet lists this weekly file as primary and the daily one as an additional upload; only the weekly file is ingested here, matching this corpus's one-file-per-diocese convention. Reconsider with Josh if a diocese having both cadences turns out to matter.
notes: Self-contained Jan 4 - Dec 20, 2026 (51 weeks) -- the source's own real scope, ending three weeks before the calendar year does; not a gap trimmed by this transcription.

'Diocesan Sta]-The Rev'd Canon Kristin Kopren...' (August 30) is a PDF text-extraction ligature corruption ('ff' misread) -- corrected to 'Diocesan Staff', per this corpus's own standing distinction between a source's own typo (preserved) and an extraction artifact (fixed), same rule already applied to this same source document's companion daily file.

Four weeks (March 22, May 31, December 6, December 13) print a named heading with a bulleted sub-list of member congregations/missions underneath it in the source's own layout -- each is recorded as ONE `category` subject (the heading as `name`) with its bulleted members preserved verbatim, semicolon-joined, in that subject's own `note`, per this session's working decision that a bullet-under-heading grouping signals one united ministry that week, distinct from the plain multi-line weeks elsewhere in the same file (which ARE split into separate subjects, one per line).

The source's own PDF line-wrapping occasionally split one sentence across a page/column break (e.g. 'Diocesan Youth Program/Camp Stoney,' wrapping onto the next line before 'The Rev'd Le Anna Brun-Missioner...'). Rejoined into complete sentences by ordinary reading, not treated as separate subjects, EXCEPT where the source's own blank-line spacing between adjacent short lines (e.g. 'Hispanic Ministries' / 'Ministry to the Displaced') signals genuinely separate subjects rather than one wrapped sentence -- judgment applied per week, not a single mechanical rule; flagged here for spot-checking.

October 11 required the most judgment of any week: the source's raw text runs 'Diocesan Youth Program/Camp Stoney, / The Rev'd Le Anna Brun-Missioner for Christian Formation The Safety and Care of all Children Bishop's Ridge, Christopher Jewell- Director' together with no reliable separator. Parsed here as three distinct `category` subjects -- 'Diocesan Youth Program/Camp Stoney, The Rev'd Le Anna Brun - Missioner for Christian Formation', 'The Safety and Care of all Children', 'Bishop's Ridge, Christopher Jewell - Director' -- by ordinary reading of where one clause/program ends and the next begins; worth a second look against the actual PDF page layout if this diocese is ever spot-checked.

Weeks naming a specific congregation ('X, City') are recorded as `parish` subjects; weeks naming a deanery, diocesan committee, ministry, or individual officer (no city given) are recorded as `category` subjects, matching this corpus's existing type distinction.
